💥 Conflicts

If conflict occurs, ping someone experienced or back up your changes

01-Topics/00-Math-Foundation/06-QA.title: 06-QA
01-Topics/00-Math-Foundation/06-QA.content:
Probability & Statistics Q&A
Q: Why can the PDF of an exponential distribution be greater than 1?
Asked in: Meeting 01
Answer: The PDF is a density, not a probability. For an exponential distribution:
f(x) = \lambda e^{-\lambda x}, \quad f(0) = \lambda
If \lambda > 1, the PDF can exceed 1. But the total probability is the area under the curve, which is always equal to 1.

Q: What does it mean for the exponential distribution to be memoryless?
Asked in: Meeting 01
Answer: The exponential distribution satisfies:
P(X > s+t \mid X > s) = P(X > t)
This means the future waiting time does not depend on how long you have already waited. The past does not affect the future because of the independence of time intervals.

Q: What does it mean for the geometric distribution to be memoryless?
Asked in: Meeting 01
Answer: The geometric distribution satisfies:
P(X > s+t \mid X > s) = P(X > t)
The proof uses the tail probability P(X > k) = (1-p)^k. Substituting:
\frac{P(X > s+t)}{P(X > s)} = \frac{(1-p)^{s+t}}{(1-p)^s} = (1-p)^t
Thus, past failures do not influence the probability of needing additional trials.

Q: What is the difference between covariance and correlation?
Asked in: Meeting 01
Answer:


Covariance: Measures how two variables change together, with units = product of their units. Range: (-\infty, +\infty).


Correlation: Standardized covariance:


\rho_{X,Y} = \frac{\text{Cov}(X, Y)}{\sigma_X \sigma_Y}
It is dimensionless, always in [-1, 1], and easier to interpret.

Q: Why is the correlation unitless?
Asked in: Meeting 01
Answer: Because dividing covariance (\text{units of } X \times Y) by \sigma_X \sigma_Y cancels the units:
\frac{\text{(kg} \cdot \text{cm)}}{\text{(kg} \cdot \text{cm)}} = 1 \text{ (unitless)}

Q: Is it valid to compare correlations from different datasets?
Asked in: Meeting 01
Answer: Yes, because correlation is standardized and unit-free, so it measures the strength of linear relationships consistently. However:

Only valid for linear relationships.
Sample size and context should be considered.

Date: 1404-04-27
Time:  8:30 PM to 10:00 PM
Facilitator: Mehrdad

📌 Agenda

 Review Probability Course Progress
 Have Discussion and Talk About Confusions
 Clarify Notes-Taking Approach
 Discuss the Site (Resource/Platform)
 Next Steps & Planning
 The Rebirth of ASP.NET


📝 Notes & Discussion

We reviewed the progress of the probability course. Participants asked several questions, which have all been answered and documented in the QA section.
Regarding the workload for next week, we agreed that watching 10 videos is too much. Instead, we will aim to watch 6 or 7 videos.
For the Hands-On Machine Learning book, the plan is to read up to page 45 and set up the development environment accordingly.
Those with available time are encouraged to start exploring Python libraries like pandas and numpy and matplotlib. Relevant resources and exercises have been shared.
On note-taking, we agreed that everyone can collect their notes individually and later merge them into a combined version. Uploading PDFs and other file types is also supported.
We discussed the site structure and future improvements;
🔥 As a symbolic act, the .NET repository was deleted during the meeting in front of everyone.
🐦‍🔥 This was followed by replacing it with a new, well-organized, cleaned-up repository — marking a rebirth of the project and a fresh start for us all.
A brief history of the .NET project was shared, covering how it started, its values, challenges faced, motivation factors, and the final project outcome.
Links to the GitHub repositories for the course, the site, and the end projects were shared, encouraging everyone to explore them.


✅ Decisions

Next week’s video watching target is set to 6-7 videos instead of 10.
Reading assignment for the Hands-On ML book is up to page 45, along with environment setup.
Members with time can begin working on Python basics (pandas, numpy, matplotlib), using the shared resources.
Note-taking will be collaborative: gather notes individually, then merge periodically.
The site structure will be updated based on feedback.

index.title: Home
index.content:
🤖 Machine Learning Study Vault
A collaborative, structured, and hands-on learning vault for Machine Learning — built by students, for students.
We follow a curated roadmap based on Hands-On Machine Learning and other top resources, focusing on shared progress, real understanding, and community-driven learning.

📘 What This Is
This repository is a living knowledge base for learning ML together.

📚 Covers core ML topics with practical focus
🧠 Includes math and Python foundations
🛠️ Features projects, notes, exercises, and tools
🗂️ Organized using Obsidian
🔄 Built to be shared, expanded, and contributed to by a group
🧱 Powered by Quartz — customized for this ML learning vault.


🧭 Roadmap
We maintain a central 📍Roadmap to track progress, topic links, learning status, and assigned tasks.
Each topic folder contains:

01-Overview.md – what the topic is about
02-Resources.md – recommended links and materials
03-CodeExamples/ – code notebooks or demos
04-Notes.md – handwritten or collaborative notes
05-Exercises.md – problems and solutions
06-Discussion.md (optional) – team thoughts or questions


📁 Folder Structure









































FolderPurpose00-GeneralRoadmap, repo structure, contribution notes01-TopicsLearning content by topic (math, ML, DL, etc.)02-PapersResearch papers and summaries03-ProjectsHands-on projects and experiments04-MeetingsMeeting notes, tasks, and planning05-TemplatesReusable templates (e.g., for meetings, overviews)06-CheatSheetsQuick reference guides and tips07-ResourcesDatasets, tools, and useful external resources

✅ Contributing

Everyone is welcome to contribute. This is a group-driven space, not a one-person show.

📌 Guidelines

Follow the existing topic structure when adding new content.
Prefer pull requests with clear commit messages.
Be kind and supportive. We’re all learning.


📄 License
This repository is open for educational use. Please respect content sources and contributors.
